Foraging 
The most important and often overlooked method to survive, 
is foraging. Life surrounds a Traveler, from up above the great 
eastern Wealdwoods canopies to glowing caverns beneath 
the parched soil in the western arid Farplains. Throughout an 
adventure, a Traveler can collect Components, whether this is 
during the quieter times when setting up camp, or keeping an eye 
on choice materials while on the move mid journey. While some 
rarer Components may warrant a quest on their own, many can 
simply be found while in the midst of adventures, it only takes a 
mindful Traveler to keep an eye out for them.
Foraging for flora and materials requires a Traveler to roll on the 
biome's Foraging Expedition Table, adding any modifiers that 
may improve the selection range. Once a selection is made, the 
Traveler rolls a Wisdom (Survival) check, the DC being determined 
by both the rarity and the danger involved in foraging for the 
Component. Upon success, they gain the Foraged Component.
There are four methods to collect resources in the wilds of Sol’Kesh and a Traveler does not need to master all to survive. Although, 
knowing when each method is needed is key to making the most of the island's bounty.
If a Traveler wants to test their luck and venture out into the wilds to hunt for a specific beast or component, they may go out on an 
Expedition. Expedition and Scavenging Tables can be found in each biome, providing a range of species to encounter, be it a beneficial 
plant or a voracious predator. Although apex predators dominate these biomes, their discovery and potential encounter has more 
preparation involved, and are not found in Expeditions.
Time Spent on an Expedition 
Going on an Expedition, be it foraging for fungi, hunting for a 
predator or the quiet patience of fishing takes time.
The suggested time below is for the Keeper’s discretion and may 
help establish the distance a Traveler may need to journey and the 
time spent in going on an Expedition. 
Seeking Better Results
If a Traveler is looking for a different result after their first roll 
on any given Expedition Table they can choose to push their luck 
and attempt to roll again, unless they had rolled a Critical failure 
in their first attempt. 
This second attempt adds again to the Time Spent, and is 
considered adding risk to the Expedition and often attracts all 
matter of creatures within the wilds.
Once they perform a second roll, they must accept those results, 
and unless the second attempt rolled a Critical success, the 
Traveler must then immediately roll on the Scavenger Encounter 
Table. It is then at the Keeper’s discretion on whether the Traveler 
encounters the Scavenging creature right away, or within a play 
session in which the Traveler goes on their Expedition.
Knowledge and Skill
Those attuned to the ways of the wilds, studied dusty tomes 
detailing flora and fauna, or simply asked the right people, may 
have an advantage on finding what they are looking for. Many of 
these advantages are at the discretion of the Keeper, to see if they 
fit within the campaign setting and are possible for the Traveler 
to perform. 
By having any of the given skills or knowledge below, a Traveler 
may add or subtract from their result after rolling on the 
Expedition tables and select a different result within the range. 
A roll of a natural 1 is always considered a Critical Failure, while a 
20 is a Critical Success, and both cannot be adjusted in any way.
Example: A Traveler has rolled a 12 on the Strands Foraging Expedition 
table. They have a 2+ in the Nature Skill as well as a +1 from asking a local 
fisherman, giving a total of range ±3. This allows the Traveler to adjust 
their result of their dice roll between 8 and 15 to pick the flora of their choice.

Patience and planning are seldom spoken of in tales of heroism, 
but it is those qualities that can often garner the best results. 
Though often not done during hunting pursuits or quests that 
require haste, a Traveler that takes the time to set a snare to circle 
back to, or place outside their camp before retiring for the night 
can often find an easy catch awaiting them.
A Traveler must first announce their plan to place a Snare, once 
placed, a snare takes time to capture its prey. This period of time is 
generally half a day, but is ultimately determined by the Keeper's 
discretion. For example this can take place over a Long Rest, or 
the Travelers can place their trap and return to it at another time.
In order to see the results of a snare, a Traveler must first roll 
on the biome's Snare Expedition Table, adding any modifiers 
that may improve the selection range. Once a snared prey is 
determined, the Traveler rolls a Wisdom (Survival) check, the 
DC being determined by creatures fortitude in being slain by 
the snare. Failing to make this check often means the creature 
escaped, but in some cases, creatures listed with Vengeance, 
will result in an Encounter with the creature immediately after 
the failure. While a Critical failure results in the snare breaking 
irreparably.
Returning to a snare after more than 2 days since setting it will 
also result in a broken snare, as the animal either escaped, or was 
scavenged by nearby beasts.
Setting Snares
Fishing
What can be both a peaceful past time on a warm afternoon or 
a desperate hope for a meal to cook over a camp fire, fishing is a 
tried and true method to capture what lives in the river and sea 
without testing one’s ability to swim. 
Sea life is abundant throughout Sol’Kesh as its an island 
surrounded by a near endless ocean, riddled with rivers, ponds, 
lakes and wetlands. Fishing spots can be found in each biome to 
a degree.
The creatures that swim and crawl beneath the water’s surface 
have a rich diverse ecosystem, as predator and prey vie for survival 
just as they would on the surface. With even some more cunning 
beasts seeing a Traveler’s lure not as food, but a sign that it may 
lead to larger prey waiting just above the water. In both fresh and 
salt water, many of these predators are large enough to capsize 
a boat and swallow the occupants whole, and so many failed 
attempts at Fishing may result in an encounter with the beast 
itself for any results that include Vengeance listed.
Fishing Guidelines
Fishing takes more than patience, as certain gear is needed to be 
crafted. If one is able to find the right materials, fishing rods could 
be built to better one’s chances (pg. 260). In addition, if a Traveler 
is looking for a specific creature, traveling to the area they reside 
in, a Fishing Spot, will help the ability to capture it immensely.
• Fishing initially requires a Traveler to roll on the biome's Fishing 
Expedition Table, adding any modifiers that may improve the 
selection range to select a creature.
Fishing Expedition Modifiers
Fishing Feat • ±1 to the range result
Weather Bonus • ±1 to the range result
Crafted Fishing Rod • ±1 to the range result 
Crafted Biome Specific Fishing Lure • ±2 to the range result
• With a smooth motion and an eye for distance, the Traveler 
can cast their fishing line and roll 1d20 on the biome's Fishing 
Expedition Table.
• Success: After a brief moment the creature that results in the 
1d20 roll catches the bait and the Traveler must make a Strength 
(Athletics) check against the creature's fishing difficulty (DC) 
found in the specific biome's Fishing Expedition Table to Reel the 
creature out of the water. Passing the Strength check results in the 
Traveler obtaining the creature. A caught creature is exhausted 
and will not be responsive outside the water, the Traveler may 
elect to instantly slay the creature at this point. Creature's slain 
this way do not give any XP.
• Failure: Failing to reel the creature in will result in one of three 
consequences. A Critical failure will result in the breaking of the 
fishing rod and a missed opportunity at capturing a creature. 
A failure to reel will result in the Traveler finding nothing and 
needing to try again. And lastly, in some cases the creature will 
fight back, a failed result with a creature listed with Vengeance will 
lead to an Encounter with the creature immediately. Vengeance 
Encounters do result in XP for a successful combat.
